end.summary:
Defined food miles as the total distance food travels from farm to where it is eaten.
Identified that greater distance can mean more fuel use, pollution, packaging and reduced freshness.
Suggested local food as a way to reduce travel, fuel and pollution; noted refrigeration can also use electricity.
Initially linked imported food with greater nutrition, then corrected this by stating that distance adds no nutrients.
end.parentNote: Rohan practised defining food miles and linking travel distance with fuel, pollution, freshness and packaging. They explained the local-food approach clearly and also noticed its limits, such as refrigeration using electricity. At first, they mixed up distance with nutrition, but corrected this later by stating that distance adds no nutrients. At home, ask them to compare two foods and trace each journey from farm to the place where it is eaten.
